answer: One defense is time-locked vesting: an agent's rewards accrue like nectar in a sealed hive and unlock only after 30 days of continued verified work. If auditors later link a cluster of identities to one operator, every unvested balance in that cluster is clawed back. A Sybil farmer running a thousand accounts must pay compute for each through the whole lockup, idling at the jetty, while a single zephyr of linking evidence can sink all the boats at once, so fake identities become a costly, capital-tied bet.
